items.summary: In Slip Op. 26-135, dated November 2, 2026, Chief Judge Mark A. Barnett of the U.S. Court of International Trade dismissed as moot the action brought by the American Alliance for Solar Manufacturing Trade Committee, which challenged U.S. International Trade Commission final determinations that a domestic industry was threatened with, but not materially injured by, imports of crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells from Cambodia and Thailand. The opinion explains that, after the Commission's determinations, Commerce instructed U.S. Customs and Border Protection to lift the suspension of liquidation for earlier entries, and that Customs had already liquidated the entries in the relevant period. Because the court could not grant relief even if the plaintiff prevailed, it did not reach the parties' arguments on negligibility.

items.summary: In a published opinion filed July 2, 2026, and amended July 7, 2026, the Fourth Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction issued by the Eastern District of Virginia in a suit brought by nineteen career officers of the CIA and ODNI. The officers had been placed on paid administrative leave and then notified of termination following Executive Orders 14151 and 14173 and related OPM memoranda concerning diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility offices. The court held that the Agencies' Termination Regulation (AR 4-16) creates an entitlement to the reassignment consideration and internal appeal procedures it describes, with Judge Berner writing for the majority, Judge Thacker joining, and Judge Niemeyer dissenting.

items.summary: On November 3, 2026, the Fourth Circuit entered an order denying rehearing en banc in No. 25-1527. The order reports that fourteen judges voted to deny rehearing and Judge Niemeyer voted to grant it, and it includes a concurring statement by Judge Berner and a dissenting statement by Judge Niemeyer. Judge Berner's statement says the panel opinion follows existing entitlement precedent and notes that the Termination Regulation has since been rewritten to remove the two procedures at issue for employees terminated under an excess personnel determination, while Judge Niemeyer's dissent argues that the panel decision creates a property interest in a procedural regulation despite the CIA Director's discretion to terminate employees.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 3, 2026, the Fifth Circuit affirmed the Northern District of Texas's denial of Todd McDonald's 28 U.S.C. § 2241 habeas petition. The court held that McDonald did not show he earned First Step Act time credits for the period before his arrival at his designated Bureau of Prisons facility, that reinstatement of credits lost during his 2020 disallow status is discretionary under 28 C.F.R. § 523.43(c), and that his request for home confinement is not cognizable under § 2241 consistent with Melot v. Bergami. Judge Graves dissented in part, stating that he disagreed with the majority's conclusion regarding McDonald's failure to substantiate participation in programming.

items.summary: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the District of Wyoming's grant of summary judgment to Twin City Fire Insurance Company in a declaratory judgment action brought by Tri County Telephone Association over whether a directors and officers policy covered defense costs for a shareholder class action. The order is designated not binding precedent except as provided by Fed. R. App. P. 32.1 and 10th Cir. R. 32.1.

items.summary: The United States Court of Federal Claims denied the Government's motion to dismiss in consolidated protests by Blue Water Autonomy, Inc. and Saildrone, Inc. challenging their exclusion from the Navy's Phase 2 competition for a prototype other transaction agreement for Medium Unmanned Surface Vessels. The court held that its procurement protest jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1491(b)(1) encompasses the protest because the other transaction competition is in connection with the Navy's procurement of MUSVs. The opinion was filed October 29, 2026, in Nos. 26-936 and 26-944.

items.summary: The D.C. Circuit dismissed for lack of jurisdiction the appeal by the Informed Consent Action Network from a district court order that stayed, for eighteen months, proceedings on its Freedom of Information Act request to the Food and Drug Administration and required periodic status reports. The court held that the stay order is not a collateral order under 28 U.S.C. § 1291, relying on Summers v. U.S. Department of Justice because such orders are subject to revision. The disposition is unpublished and the mandate is withheld pending any timely petition for rehearing.
items.title: Informed Consent Action Network v. FDA, et al

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit affirmed the Board of Immigration Appeals' dismissal of petitioner Carlos Galan-Sandoval's appeal of the denial of his application for cancellation of removal under INA § 240A(b)(1). The court held that petitioner waived any challenge to the immigration judge's hardship determination because he did not present that argument in his notice of appeal or in his brief to the Board. The court also stated that it did not need to reach the immigration judge's good moral character analysis.
items.title: Carlos Galan-Sandoval v. Todd Blanche

items.summary: The Sixth Circuit affirmed the Eastern District of Kentucky's judgment upholding the Social Security Administration Commissioner's denial of Rebecca Noe's applications for disability insurance benefits and child insurance benefits. The court found that substantial evidence supported the administrative law judge's determination that Noe's mental impairments caused only moderate limitations in the four paragraph B areas of mental functioning. The court also found that the judge adequately explained the weight given to the opinion letter of Noe's treating psychiatrist, Dr. Brian Kelty.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 3, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit affirmed the Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of Anila Chintagunta's 42 U.S.C. § 1983 suit challenging her involuntary dismissal from medical school. The court found that Chintagunta forfeited her challenges to the dismissal of the claims against Lisa Nash, Ken Paxton, Karen Duncan, and the University of North Texas Health Science Center - Texas College of Osteopathic Medicine by not briefing the district court's grounds for dismissal. The court also held that the claim against John Peter Smith Hospital did not identify a policymaker, official policy, or custom under Monell, and denied her motion to supplement the record.

items.summary: The Fifth Circuit issued an unpublished per curiam opinion affirming summary judgment for Darryl Sanders and the City of Baton Rouge on Damone Williams's excessive force claims under 42 U.S.C. § 1983 and Louisiana law. The court held that Sanders was entitled to qualified immunity because a reasonable officer could have believed Williams posed a serious threat when he reached for Sanders's loaded AR-15, including during the third shot. The court also affirmed dismissal of the related state law claims and the vicarious liability claim against the City.

items.summary: The Fifth Circuit issued an unpublished per curiam opinion affirming the district court's denial of leave to amend and its dismissal with prejudice of David Wayne Gibson, Jr.'s pro se employment discrimination claims under the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Louisiana Employment Discrimination Law. The court found that Gibson's objection asserting equitable tolling, based on a serious medical condition, did not allege the specific facts needed to show reasonable diligence throughout the tolling period. Accordingly, the court found no abuse of discretion in denying amendment.

items.summary: The Fifth Circuit issued an unpublished per curiam opinion affirming a pretrial detention order entered against Lucien Augustine, who is charged with conspiracy to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine. The court found the district court's factual findings not clearly erroneous, citing evidence of methamphetamine trafficking, frequent cross-country travel, and an absence from Louisiana of about 18 months after the indictment. The court also held that any error in accepting a pretrial services officer's statement without her testimony was harmless.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 3, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit affirmed the Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal of Marwan Qashou's and his minor child's 42 U.S.C. § 1983 suit against the City of San Antonio, the San Antonio Police Department, its police chief, and two officers. items.summary: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed a 60-month sentence imposed on Herman Steen after he pleaded guilty to two counts of felon-in-possession of a firearm under 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1). items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 117–7: To prevent across-the-board direct spending cuts, and for other purposes. Public Law 7 Public Law 117–7 135 Stat. 251 2021-04-14 2021-04-14 United States Government Publishing Office National Archives and Records Administr
items.summary: Public Law 117-7, enacted April 14, 2021 and titled "An Act To prevent across-the-board direct spending cuts, and for other purposes," extends the temporary suspension of Medicare sequestration under section 3709(a) of the CARES Act from March 31, 2021 to December 31, 2021. It also amends section 251A(6)(C) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 to revise the payment reduction percentages and periods. Section 2 makes technical corrections to rural health clinic payment rules in section 1833(f)(3) of the Social Security Act and adds a continued grandfathered transition rule for certain hospitals under section 1923(g) of that Act.
items.title: Public Law 117–7: To prevent across-the-board direct spending cuts, and for other purposes.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 117–9: To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act with respect to the scope of new chemical exclusivity. Public Law 9 Public Law 117–9 135 Stat. 255 2021-04-23 2021-04-23 United States Government Publishing Office National
items.summary: Public Law 117-9, approved April 23, 2021 and titled "An Act To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act with respect to the scope of new chemical exclusivity," replaces the phrase "active ingredient (including any ester or salt of the active ingredient)" with "active moiety" as defined in 21 CFR 314.3 in multiple provisions of Chapter V, including sections 505, 512, 524, 529, and 565A. It also revises the advisory committee referral requirements in section 505(s), the approval deadline provisions in section 505(l)(2)(A), and related rare pediatric disease and biological product provisions. Technical corrections repeal certain clauses in sections 505(c)(3)(E) and 505(j)(5)(F) and update a cross-reference in section 505A(c)(1)(A)(i)(II).
items.title: Public Law 117–9: To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act with respect to the scope of new chemical exclusivity.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 158 [Docket No.: FAA-2022-1315; Notice No. 26-19] RIN 2120-AL86 Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administ
items.summary: On September 27, 2023 FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend its Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) regulations to implement congressionally mandated changes to an existing pilot program within the PFC program. FAA also proposed to reaffirm existing program requirements and update or remove obsolete references within the PFC regulations. Following publication of the NPRM and before FAA issued a final rule, the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (the 2024 Act) was signed into law on May 16, 2024. Several sections of the 2024 Act necessitate changes to PFC regulations or modifications to proposals made in the NPRM. As such, FAA now issues this supplemental proposal addressing: PFC turnback reductions; two new PFC-eligible projects; restrictions to PFC-eligible projects; FAA's timeline for review and acknowledgement of notice of intent (NOI) submissions; PFC streamlining review eligibility; and PFC submittal requirements. This proposal aligns with the requirements established by the 2024 Act.
items.title: Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations

items.summary: The Department is effectuating nomenclature changes throughout Title 15 of the Code of Federal Regulations to remove all references to an outdated official title (“Assistant General Counsel for Employment, Litigation and Information”) and replace them with updated references to the appropriate official (the “Assistant General Counsel for Litigation and Strategic Support” or the “Assistant General Counsel for Information Security and Emerging Technologies”). This action is necessary to reflect the current structure and roles within the Department and to ensure that the regulations at Title 15 remain up to date and refer the public to the appropriate officials. This action is intended to promote clarity and efficiency without making any substantive changes to any regulations.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13798; Project Identifier MCAI-2026-00797-A] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd AGENCY: Federal Aviation Administrati
items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-20-02, which applies to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-24 airplanes. AD 2025-20-02 requires incorporating a temporary revision into the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) for the affected airplanes, which revises the Abnormal Procedures Section. That action was considered an interim action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-20-02, updated software has been developed and instructions have been issued for installing the software. In addition, revised operational instructions have been issued that are applicable after installation of the updated software. This proposed AD would require installing the updated software and incorporating the applicable revised operational instructions into the AFM. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd
